Definition: the weeping tree (some gum-distilling tree, perhaps the balsam)
BiblicalUsage: Baka is the weeping tree — the mulberry, or balsam, the tree that weeps gum. David heard the sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees, and knew it was the sign to go up against the Philistines, because the Lord had gone out before him. The trees were the signal, and the victory followed.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God still gives his people a sound in the tops of the trees — a sign to move, when he himself has gone out before them. David waited for it, and I mean to wait for mine.
